overview.title: Exchange Rate Policy
overview.definition: Exchange rate policy refers to the strategy and framework adopted by a central bank and government to manage their currency's value relative to other foreign currencies, balancing macroeconomic stability, trade competitiveness, and capital account openness.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC Civil Services Prelims (questions on RBI interventions, Managed Float, REER vs. NEER, Capital Convertibility) and Mains GS Paper 3 (Economy - External Sector, Export Competitiveness, Forex Reserves management).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Exchange Rate Policy in India.
Evaluate spatial distribution of forex reserves, RBI intervention tools, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions on REER/NEER and exchange rate regimes.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Managed Floating Exchange Rate Regime**: India follows a **market-determined exchange rate system** since 1993 (Tarapore Committee recommendations), where the RBI does not target any fixed exchange rate but intervenes in the foreign exchange market only to curb **excessive volatility** and disorderly market conditions.
• **Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER)**: Measures the value of a home currency against a basket of foreign currencies without adjusting for inflation differentials.
• **Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER)**: NEER adjusted for inflation differentials between the home country and its trading partners; serves as a key indicator of **external trade competitiveness**.
• **Key Objective**: Maintaining exchange rate stability in line with economic fundamentals, preventing speculative attacks, and ensuring adequate **Foreign Exchange Reserves (FER)** cushion.

items.definition: The process by which the RBI neutralizes the monetary impact of its forex market interventions (buying/selling dollars) through the open market sale/purchase of government securities (OMO) to control domestic money supply and inflation.

Landmark committees appointed by the RBI on **Capital Account Convertibility (CAC)**, setting strict pre-conditions like fiscal deficit reduction, lower inflation, and robust forex reserves before full CAC.
Replaced FERA; aimed at facilitating external trade and payments and promoting orderly development and maintenance of the foreign exchange market in India.

US Department of Treasury watchlist tracking major trading partners with significant bilateral trade surpluses and material current account surpluses; India has been occasionally included due to net forex purchases.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Financial Hubs**: Mumbai (Bandra-Kurla Complex, GIFT City in Gandhinagar) serving as the core centres for onshore and offshore rupee trading (NDFs).
• **Trade Basket Geography**: India's NEER/REER calculations incorporate a trade-weighted basket of major currencies including the US Dollar, Euro, Chinese Yuan, UAE Dirham, and Japanese Yen.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Imported inflation due to rupee depreciation, capital flight during US Fed rate hikes, and trade deficit pressures.
• **Policy Interventions**: Internationalizing the Indian Rupee (INR for trade settlement), bilateral swap arrangements, and deepening domestic financial markets.

items.title: Mnemonic for REER vs. NEER Distinction
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "REER has Real Inflation Feel".
• **Decoded Meaning**: NEER is Nominal (no inflation adjustment), while REER accounts for relative inflation (Real).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly distinguishes statements regarding trade competitiveness vs. nominal currency value.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Depreciation of Rupee = Exports cheaper/competitive + Imports costlier (Inflationary pressure).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often frames statements claiming 'India follows a Fixed Exchange Rate system' or 'RBI targets a specific Rupee-Dollar exchange rate like 80 INR/USD'. Both are incorrect; India follows a flexible, market-determined managed float without any fixed target.

Mains Value Addition: In GS Paper 3, analyze how RBI's forex intervention balances the 'Impossible Trinity' (Trilemma) of international economics—choosing between independent monetary policy, exchange rate stability, and capital mobility.

keyTakeaways: India operates a Managed Floating exchange rate regime where the RBI intervenes solely to curb excessive volatility, not to fix the rupee's value.
REER is the key metric for export competitiveness as it adjusts the Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) for inflation differentials.
Sterilization via Open Market Operations (OMOs) allows the RBI to manage forex inflows without losing control over domestic inflation.
